time_convention: t = frame / 24; frame 0 at t = 0; time t -> frame round(t*24)

active_image_px.note: black pillarbox bars at x<160 and x>2719; rendered picture is 2560x1440 (16:9). Its centre (1439.5, 719.5) equals the full-frame centre; take the principal point there. If a field-of-view figure is ever used, it most likely refers to the 2560 px rendered width.

units: pixels and seconds; no metric scale estimated

camera.evidence: phase correlation of background patches vs frame 0 over all frames: shifts < 0.3 px (scripts/cam.py)
camera.view: oblique high view looking down onto a snowy/rocky canyon terrain; no horizon or sky in frame (terrain fills the top edge). Ground recedes upward in the image (top = farther). No straight man-made lines, so no clean vanishing points.

objects.name: dragon
objects.description: single dark grey winged dragon (wyvern-type: two hind legs, two large brown-grey membrane wings, long tail); the only moving object
objects.fully_in_frame: all frames (bbox never touches the active-image edge)
objects.reference_point: ref_x, ref_y = pelvis/hip (top of hind legs at the tail base), hand-marked on frames 0,4,...,64,71 and template-tracked in between; best available proxy for the rig root. Accuracy about +-10-15 px (worse, +-20-30 px, during the flapping frames 14-22 and 36-45 when the body is seen from behind/below).
objects.image_path_summary: moves right-to-left and up the image (away from the camera): ref (2115,985) at f0 -> (1614,703) f24 -> (1325,533) f44 -> (1220,433) f52 -> (1030,353) f71. Ref path length (sum of per-frame steps) about 1358 px; net 1256 px.

wing_pose_phases.pose: wings raised (upstroke top / start of downstroke), mask large: bbox ~1144x786 at f0
wings swept level/low, widest horizontal spread of the flapping phase: bbox_w 1045-1050, bbox_h ~321-345 (f13-14)
wings down/forward, body seen from below-behind, bbox_w minimum ~477 (f17)
wings level: bbox_w 868 at f37, bbox_h 243
wings down, body seen from behind, bbox_w minimum 359 at f42
wings spread out; from about f51/52 to the end the dragon glides with an almost fixed pose (wings held spread, legs hanging, tail trailing down-right)

apparent_size.note: with the pose nearly fixed from f52 to f71 the bbox shrinks ~14% (748 -> 642 px): the dragon is moving away from the camera (depth grows roughly 1/0.86 = 1.17x over 0.83 s). During flapping (f0-50) bbox size is dominated by the wing pose, not by depth.
apparent_size.max_wingspan_like_extent_px: largest horizontal mask extent while wings are level: f13-14 ~1045-1050 px; f25-26 ~932-956; f37 ~868; glide f52 ~748 (depth changes between these frames, so compare with care)
apparent_size.body_only_size_px_approx: frame 56 (glide), read by eye from a gridded crop, +-15 px: head ~(1130,355), hip ~(1180,423), tail tip ~(1320,535), feet ~(1180,480); head-to-hip ~85 px, hip-to-tail-tip ~180 px, head-to-tail-tip ~270 px (projected, the body is foreshortened); wing tips at f56 set the mask bbox x-range 818-1546 (bbox y 216-538)

objects.name: dragon_shadow
objects.description: the dragon's cast shadow on the terrain (dark, soft-edged, broken up by rocks); sunlight from the upper right so the shadow lies below-left of the dragon in the image
objects.reliability: low: centroid/bbox of the segmented shadow fragments; jumps when fragments appear/disappear on the rough terrain; in frames 38-47 and 52-71 parts of the shadow lying close to the dragon may be missing or partly assigned to the dragon

objects.name: terrain
objects.description: static eroded rock/snow canyon covering the whole picture: pale pink-white rock blocks with vertical streaks, a smoother sandy flat in the lower right, dark rock face on the far right edge (x~2500-2720, y~350-1000)
objects.notes: no distinct props, people, vehicles or markings. A small isolated dark spike/rock at about (2690,1240) near the right edge.

events.event: clip start; frames 0 and 1 are pixel-identical (duplicated first frame), so the image shows no motion between them
dragon's shadow enters the bottom edge of the frame
wings level at end of first downstroke (widest horizontal spread)
ref point stops moving sideways-flat and starts climbing steeply in the image (y 906 at f14 -> 726 at f20)
ref y local minimum (623): body dips slightly down in the image until f36-37 (y 648) during the third downstroke, then climbs again
shadow fully inside the frame from here on
last wing stroke ends; glide with fixed wing pose until the end (f51/52-71); ref moves smoothly up-left, slowing slightly
clip end; dragon still in view

no_contacts: the dragon never touches the ground or any object; no release, bounce or impact events
